process_area.title: Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup

value_stream.name: Trade Accounts Receivable Factoring, Invoice Discounting & Receivables Securitization

workflows.name: Receivables Financing Strategy, Instrument Selection & Working-Capital Plan

Automation Opportunity: - AR-aging and DSO analytics auto-fed into the funding-gap and instrument-evaluation model.
Controls: - CTL-797: ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).) — strategy/facility approval; CTL-21 (working-capital-data accuracy; CTL-35 (budget/funding-plan adherence).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury), VS-16/VS-68 (AR/credit), VS-105 (SCF), VS-170 (ABL), VS-36 (board)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Instrument-mismatch risk**: choosing recourse factoring when the goal was risk transfer leaves BuildRight holding the credit risk and paying factor fees; mitigated by clear objective-setting in the strategy.
- **Over-reliance risk**: depending solely on factoring for working capital concentrates funding risk on the factor; mitigated by a diversified funding mix (VS-18/VS-170).
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/funding module (VS-18); AR aging (VS-16/VS-68); working-capital analytics (VS-105/VS-170).
Time Estimate: - ~5 weeks elapsed per annual refresh; ~100–200 person-hours of named-owner effort within that window (step durations are elapsed windows, not contiguous effort).

steps.activity: Quantify the trade-receivables balance and cash-conversion cycle from AR aging (VS-16/VS-68) and the funding gap.
Evaluate instruments: recourse factoring, non-recourse factoring (credit-insured), invoice discounting (confidential), and securitization — on cost, risk transfer, and customer-impact.
Select the target funding mix (e.g. factoring for high-risk segments, discounting for investment-grade accounts) and target advance rates.
Build the business case: funding cost vs. DSO/cash-release benefit vs. risk transfer vs. relationship cost.
Approve at the treasury/credit committee and align to the group funding plan (VS-18) and board reporting (VS-36).

workflows.name: Factor/Funder Selection, Facility Negotiation & Master Factoring Agreement

Automation Opportunity: - Covenant dashboard with early-warning on dilution/concentration ratios.
Controls: - CTL-797: ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).) — facility authorization; CTL-21 (covenant compliance; CTL-19 (treasury reconciliation).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury/facility), VS-100 (legal/contracts), VS-170 (ABL alternatives)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Covenant-breach risk**: breaching a facility covenant (dilution ratio, concentration) triggers termination/recourse; mitigated by covenant monitoring and early corrective action.
- **Funder-concentration risk**: a single funder withdrawing leaves the program unfunded; mitigated by multiple funder relationships where scale allows.
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/funding module (VS-18); factoring facility master; covenant compliance (VS-18 W319); contract management (VS-100).
Time Estimate: - ~6–8 weeks elapsed per facility negotiation; ~1 day/month ongoing.

steps.activity: RFP/qualify factors/funders (banks, specialized AR financiers) on pricing, advance rate, recourse terms, and service.
Negotiate facility terms: discount/fee rate, advance rate, recourse period, concentration limits, and termination.
Legal review and execute the master factoring/discounting agreement (assignment, representations, covenants).
Configure the facility in the treasury/factoring system with limits, rates, and recourse terms.
Onboard to drawdown (W5401) and monitor covenant compliance (VS-18).

workflows.name: Eligible-Receivable Criteria, Concentration Limits & Advance-Rate Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Automated eligibility-gating and concentration checks at invoice submission.
Controls: - CTL-797 (ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).)
- operational: eligibility accuracy; fraud detection on fabricated invoices; concentration-limit adherence; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR), VS-68 (credit/limits), VS-125 (fraud on receivables)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ineligible-submission risk**: submitting ineligible receivables (over-age, disputed, over-limit) triggers funder rejection and fees; mitigated by automated eligibility-gating at submission.
- **Concentration-breach risk**: breaching a concentration limit triggers funder recourse/termination; mitigated by concentration monitoring and limits.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring eligibility engine; AR/credit module (VS-16/VS-68); concentration/dilution analytics.
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks elapsed setup; ~1 week per quarterly review.

steps.activity: Define eligible-receivable criteria: approved customers, credit-insured/non-recourse eligibility, invoice age, and disputed-free.
Set concentration limits (max per customer, segment, region) and advance rates (e.g. 80–90% investment-grade, 70% others).
Configure the criteria/limits/advance rates in the factoring system to gate eligibility at submission (W5401).
Monitor dilution (credits/disputes/short-pays as % of sales) against facility thresholds.
Review and adjust criteria/limits quarterly based on portfolio performance (W5410).

fields.Frequency: Setup; per newly enrolled customer segment
fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager (VS-107), Legal (VS-100), Credit Manager, Marketing/Comms (VS-14)

workflows.name: Customer Notification Strategy (Notification vs. Silent/Confidential Factoring)

Automation Opportunity: - Per-segment notification templates and remit-to auto-update.
Controls: - CTL-27: customer data on notifications; CTL-797 (ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).) — assignment legal sign-off; CTL-21 (remit-to accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-107 (key accounts), VS-14 (comms), VS-100 (legal/assignment), VS-29 (master data)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Relationship-damage risk**: notifying customers of factoring can signal financial distress and harm relationships; mitigated by silent/confidential discounting for sensitive segments and careful communication.
- **Invalid-assignment risk**: a notification that fails legal assignment requirements leaves the sale unenforceable; mitigated by legal review of notification/assignment language (W5400).
System Touchpoints: - Customer master remit-to (VS-29); factoring notification records; lockbox (W5398); AR (VS-16).
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks elapsed setup; per-segment communication ongoing.

steps.activity: Decide per segment: notification factoring (customer pays the factor) vs. silent/confidential discounting (customer pays BuildRight, which remits).
For notification factoring: draft customer notification and remit-to change; legal review for assignment validity (W5400).
Coordinate customer communication with Trade Account Management to manage relationship impact (VS-107/VS-14).
Set up the remit-to instruction and lockbox (W5398) for notified customers.
Monitor customer payment behavior post-notification (W5411).

workflows.name: Receivables Sale Accounting Design, True-Sale/Off-Balance-Sheet Opinion & Derecognition (PFRS 9)

Automation Opportunity: - Recourse/substance analytics flag changes that could re-characterize the sale (W5415).
Controls: - CTL-31: adequate provisions/recourse reserve; CTL-29 (consolidated reporting); CTL-21 (accounting accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-157 (revenue/contract accounting), VS-17 (GL), VS-21 (audit), VS-100 (legal opinion)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Re-characterization risk**: a "sale" that is in substance a secured borrowing (excessive recourse, no true transfer) stays on-balance-sheet and distorts leverage/EBITDA and the audited PFRS financials; mitigated by true-sale opinion and substance monitoring.
- **Audit-qualification risk**: an unsupported derecognition policy risks audit qualification; mitigated by external-auditor agreement and documented policy.
System Touchpoints: - GL/revenue-recognition (VS-17/VS-157); factoring accounting module; auditor workpapers (VS-21).
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks elapsed setup; ~1 week per annual audit confirmation.

steps.activity: Design the receivables-sale accounting: derecognition (PFRS 9) vs. secured borrowing, based on whether control/risks transferred.
Obtain a true-sale / off-balance-sheet legal opinion (recourse structure permitting).
Configure GL/accounting for the sale, recourse reserve, and factor-fee/interest treatment (VS-17/VS-157).
Document the policy and obtain external-auditor agreement at the annual audit.
Monitor for changes in substance (recourse activity, W5407) that could re-characterize the sale (W5415).

workflows.name: Factoring/Securitization Platform, Lockbox & Remittance Infrastructure Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Full straight-through processing: eligible invoice → auto-submit → drawdown → lockbox → reconciliation.
Controls: - CTL-19: bank/lockbox reconciliation; CTL-21 (integration accuracy); CTL-27 (customer remit data).
Cross-references: - links to VS-27 (IT/integration), VS-16 (AR), VS-18 (treasury/bank), VS-29 (master data)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Integration-failure risk**: a broken AR↔factoring↔lockbox link causes missed drawdowns and mis-applied cash; mitigated by end-to-end testing and reconciliation (W5404).
- **Mis-directed-payment risk**: a customer paying BuildRight instead of the factor (or vice-versa) under a notification setup; mitigated by clear remit-to instructions and lockbox controls.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring platform; lockbox/bank (VS-18); AR integration (VS-16); customer master remit-to (VS-29); IT integration (VS-27).

steps.activity: Set up the factoring/securitization platform: invoice submission, drawdown, reconciliation, and reporting modules.
Establish the lockbox/bank-account infrastructure for customer remittance to the factor (notification) or BuildRight (silent).
Integrate AR (VS-16) ↔ factoring platform ↔ lockbox for eligibility, submission, and cash application.
Configure remit-to instructions and customer notifications per W5396.
Test end-to-end (invoice→drawdown→customer payment→reconciliation) before go-live.

workflows.name: Dilution, Reserve & Holdback Modeling, and Credit-Protection/Insurance Sourcing

Automation Opportunity: - Dilution auto-computed from AR credits/disputes; reserve auto-sized.
Controls: - CTL-797 (ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).)
- operational: dilution accuracy; adequate reserve; coverage; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-68 (trade credit risk/insurance), VS-26 (insurance), VS-17 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-reserved risk**: a reserve too small for actual dilution leaves BuildRight covering shortfalls from recourse/holdback; mitigated by dilution modeling and periodic review.
- **Uninsured non-recourse risk**: non-recourse factoring without credit insurance transfers risk back on funder default; mitigated by credit-protection sourcing.
System Touchpoints: - Credit-risk/dilution analytics (VS-68); trade-credit insurance (VS-68/VS-26); factoring reserve accounting (VS-17).
Time Estimate: - ~3 weeks elapsed setup; ~1 week per quarterly review.

steps.activity: Model portfolio dilution (credits/disputes/short-pays as % of sales) to size the reserve/holdback.
Structure the factor reserve/holdback (a % of advance held back against dilution/default).
For non-recourse: source trade-credit insurance/credit-protection (VS-68) covering the factored receivables.
Configure the reserve/holdback and insurance into the facility and accounting (W5397).
Review dilution/loss experience vs. model and adjust reserve/insurance periodically (W5410).

workflows.name: BSP/SEC Compliance, Truth-in-Lending & Assignment-Notification Legal Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Assignment-notification templates and AML screening integrated into submission.
Controls: - CTL-208: BSP/SEC & truth-in-lending statutory compliance (regulatory reporting and registration); CTL-797 (ensure controlled execution — Receivables Financing Strategy, Funder Relationships & Program Setup (PA-189.1).) — assignment legal sign-off; CTL-27 (customer data).
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-100 (legal), VS-86 (AML), VS-88 (records), VS-79 (tax on financing income)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Invalid-assignment risk**: a receivables sale not validly assigned/perfected is unenforceable against the customer and other creditors; mitigated by documented assignment legal requirements.
- **Regulatory-action risk**: conducting regulated financing without registration triggers SEC/BSP action; mitigated by confirming the regulatory vehicle.
System Touchpoints: - Regulatory reporting; assignment/notification records (VS-88); AML (VS-86); compliance monitoring (VS-22).

steps.activity: Confirm any regulatory registration/reporting for the receivables-financing activity (SEC/BSP where applicable).
Establish valid-assignment legal requirements (notice, writing, perfection) for the receivables sale.
Ensure Truth-in-Lending (RA 3765) disclosure where financing charges apply to customers.
Set up AML screening on factoring funds/counterparties (VS-86) and records retention (VS-88).
Monitor regulatory changes and audit compliance (VS-22/VS-21).
